To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the preprocessing of MS/2 spectra is an effective means for increasing the sensitivity and specificity of peptide identification and that (2) preprocessing methods that are based on a probabilistic model of MS/MS peaks are superior to those that are not.

(1) preprocessing MS/MS spectra with MS‐deisotoper, MS‐deisotope‐filter or MS‐deisotope‐filter‐filter‐deisotope is the optimal preprocessing for the majority of the data sets and (2) the optimal preprocessing depends on the data set, the number of spectra, the type of mass spectrometer, the type of fragmentation, and the database size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of efficient algorithms for the preprocessing of MS/ML spectra.
the development and evaluation of MS/MS preprocessing tools.
the development and evaluation of methods to preprocess MS/MS spectra prior to database searches for peptide identification.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
no one method is the best for every data set.
no single method is best for all data sets and that the choice of the preprocessing method should be based on the data type.
there are no clear winners or losers, and no one method can be recommended over another.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the best preprocessing methods for MS/MS spectra are those that are most conservative, that is, they remove the least amount of peaks, and that they use a combination of several peak selection methods.

the preprocessing of MS/ MS spectra with the software package MSPrep (http://www.childrenshospita.org/research/steeneb) can improve the performance of Mascot, Sequestr and ProteinPilot significantly, and is a useful tool to reduce file size and run time for large scale proteomic data sets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of the preprocessing method depends on the data set and the search algorithm.
preprocessing of MS/ MS spectra can increase the number of correctly identified peptides significantly and reduce the number of false positives.
the best performance is achieved by combining multiple preprocessing methods.
